# [CS020] Weak Hash Algorithm (crypto-weak-hash)

MD5 or SHA-1 is used for a security purpose, or a fast hash stores passwords.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-328](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/328.html) |
| **OWASP** | A04:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

MD5 and SHA-1 have practical collisions, and any fast hash lets attackers test billions of password guesses per second. Use SHA-256 or SHA-3 for integrity and bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2id for passwords.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
sum := md5.Sum([]byte(password))
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
hash, err := bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword([]byte(password), bcrypt.DefaultCost)
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [crypto-weak-hash]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    crypto-weak-hash: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore crypto-weak-hash -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** crypto-weak-hash
```
